saints.name: St. Catherine de’ Ricci
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: A Dominican prioress of Prato favored with weekly ecstasies of the Lord’s Passion, and a counselor of saints and popes by her letters…
biography: Alessandra de' Ricci was born at Florence in 1522 of a patrician family. At thirteen she entered the Dominican convent of San Vincenzo at Prato, taking the name Catherine, and after early trials borne with patience she rose to be prioress, an office she filled for more than thirty years.

In February 1542 she was first seized by the great 'Ecstasy of the Passion,' in which, from Thursday noon until four o'clock on Friday, she relived the sufferings of Christ and bore their marks in her flesh. The ecstasy returned week by week for twelve years, ceasing in 1554 in answer to the prayers of the community, whose quiet was broken by the crowds it drew.

Her counsel was sought far beyond the cloister: she corresponded with Philip Neri — to whom, it was believed, she once appeared without leaving her convent — and with three cardinals who became popes, Marcellus II, Leo XI, and Clement VIII.

She died at Prato on 2 February 1590 and was canonized in 1746 by Pope Benedict XIV. Having borne the pains of Christ in her own body and tended the suffering with gentleness, she is invoked as a patron of the sick.
saints.knownFor: Her mystical ecstasies of Christ’s Passion.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 13 February
